newsitem.title: UK: Britain blocks Bass merger with Carlsberg-Tetley.
newsitem.headline: Britain blocks Bass merger with Carlsberg-Tetley.

text.p: British authorities Friday blocked the proposed merger between brewing and hotel giant Bass Plc and Carlsberg-Tetley, shocking investors and analysts, who had been expecting approval.
The deal would have made Bass Britain's biggest brewer, handing it 35 percent of the domestic beer market.

Margaret Beckett, the Labour government's new Trade and Industry Secretary, said in a statement that she disagreed with the Monopolies and Mergers Commission view that the negative effects of the merger could be dealt with by demanding the sale of 1,900 Bass pubs.
"I am not persuaded that the divestment of 1,900 pubs would be an adequate counterweight to the substantial strengthening of Bass's position as a producer and wholesaler of beer," she said.
Bass and Carlsberg had no immediate comment, although each said it was in the process of drawing up a response.
Bass' existing market share is 23 percent, below Scottish and Newcastle Plc, which makes 29 of every 100 pints consumed.
Taking the hardest line in her first major ruling on competition issues, Beckett said she was seeking an undertaking from Bass to sell its existing 50 percent stake in Carlsberg-Tetley.

Beckett said "Bass's acquisition of Carlsberg-Tetley would represent a further substantial step in the direction of concentration in an industry that has already seen a number of national brewers with tied estates fall from six to four since 1989."
This referred to the British brewing industry's system under which pubs are allowed to sell only beer that their parent company has brewed.
The news was greeted with surprise in the market. Bass shares rose strongly, while Carlsberg shares fell in Copenhagen

Nick Lyle, brewing analyst at SocGen, said "I'm a bit taken aback. We had expected to see the deal to be tied to harsh conditions rather than completely blocked. It must be frustrating for Bass, but it won't have lost a lot of cash on this."
Under the original terms of the deal, announced last August, Bass paid 200 million pounds ($333 million) for the 50 percent interest in Carlsberg-Tetley owned by drinks group Allied Domecq.

Carlsberg, the Danish brewer that held the rest, agreed to contribute its interest to Bass, together with 20 million pounds ($33 million), in exchange for 20 percent of the merged Bass Brewers/Carlsberg-Tetley business.
